news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway: Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary allocation left a gap of about £10m
news_drafts.lead:
The money Dumfries and Galloway Council had agreed for Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary School does not cover the costs identified for the two schools, leaving a funding gap of around £10m. The figure is in an appendix to the council's capital investment programme, its planned spending on things that last, such as buildings, over the next few years.

The council's Education and Learning Committee agreed on 23 May 2024 that the existing allocation was not enough. That allocation is part of £73.975m in the programme. The appendix says: "Previously agreed capital allocation (part of the £73.975m) is not enough to cover the values identified, so Members also agreed to request the funding gap, circa £10m, from FTP committee."

FTP is the Finance, Procurement and Transformation Committee. The papers quoted here do not say how that committee responded to the request.

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway council secures £50m Levelling Up grants but faces social care audit concerns
news_drafts.lead: The council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund. Its capital projects — spending on buildings and other long-lived assets — are delivering on schedule: the Stranraer Watersports Hub is due to open in September, the Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels facility is nearing completion, and the George building has attracted eight expressions of interest with a tender exercise in progress. The internal audit's overall opinion is Reasonable, meaning there is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place. However, auditors have flagged two areas requiring ongoing monitoring: social care budgets and IT procurement, indicating these carry elevated risk requiring continuous attention.

news_drafts.headline: SWestrans governance audit actions nine months overdue as oversight gaps widen
news_drafts.lead: The South West of Scotland Transport Partnership has failed to complete two fundamental governance audit actions nine months past their December 2025 deadline. Financial Regulations and Codes on the partnership's website remain from 2006, and a Scheme of Delegation has not been published. Both are essential to financial control and governance. The failures coincide with growing operational pressures: staff costs have overrun by £164,000 (with £146,000 of confirmed additional funding from Dumfries and Galloway Council and the remainder unresolved), and fuel prices have risen 33.5% year-on-year. The partnership forecasts a modest £54,000 underspend but acknowledges material inflation and demand risks that could reverse it. On capital spending, monthly monitoring against profiled budgets is being introduced after the partnership discovered a £1,046,795 underspend, partly because annual reporting failed to surface emerging variances. Of that underspend, £525,000 in Active Travel Infrastructure Fund grant must be committed by 31 March 2027 or be lost.

findings.headline: Structures has a 2026/27 forecast outturn of £599,428 against a £480,000 revised budget, a forecast variance of £119,428.
findings.detail: Actual net spend to date is £54,112. The forecast variance is shown as £119,428, with a 2027/28 indicative budget of £360,000.
findings.matters: A forecast above budget on a structures programme is a cost pressure that finance officers at other councils with similar bridge and structures work will recognise.
findings.figures: £480,000 revised budget; £54,112 actual net spend to date; £599,428 forecast outturn; £119,428 forecast variance; £360,000 indicative 2027/28

findings.headline: LUF Multi Modal Transport Hubs shows £4,699,140 of income to date against £1,903,382 of actual expenditure.
findings.detail: The LUF Multi Modal Transport Hubs line records actual net spend to date of (£2,795,758), meaning grant income exceeds spend. The line's total project external funding is £6,633,100.
findings.matters: Grant received well ahead of spend is cash the council holds for later costs, and a peer council with a similar LUF award can compare how it is timed.
findings.figures: £6,633,100 total project external funding; £1,903,382 actual expenditure to date; £4,699,140 actual income to date; (£2,795,758) actual net spend to date

findings.headline: Two virements to Stranraer Marina, of £250,000 and £800,000, appear in the Economic Development and Public Realm funding summaries.
findings.detail: The Economic Development summary records a £250,000 virement to Stranraer Marina. The Public Realm summary records an £800,000 virement to the same project, reducing the Public Realm total budget.
findings.matters: Moving capital between asset classes to fund a single project is a reallocation decision a finance director would want to see recorded and approved.
findings.figures: (£250,000) Economic Development virement; (£800,000) Public Realm virement; £1,050,000 combined

findings.headline: The Property Schools funding summary records RAAC re-profiling of (£2,200,000) against an additional RAAC funding line of £2,000,000 for 2026/27.
findings.detail: The RAAC Works to Schools block has a revised 2026/27 budget of £1,763,363 with £497,975 actual spend to date. The funding summary shows the RAAC re-profiling as a deduction from the base budget.
findings.matters: RAAC remediation in schools is a national capital pressure, and a council reprofiling a RAAC budget is a timing signal that peers and lenders can compare with their own RAAC programmes.
findings.figures: £2,000,000 additional RAAC funding; (£2,200,000) RAAC re-profiling; £1,763,363 revised RAAC Works to Schools budget; £497,975 actual spend to date

findings.headline: Calside Primary School heating upgrade and window replacement is forecast at £400,000 against a £600,000 budget, with £200,000 shown as indicative 2027/28 budget.
findings.detail: Actual expenditure to date is £11,251 and the forecast variance is (£200,000). The 2027/28 indicative budget column carries £200,000 for the same project.
findings.matters: A schools heating project moving part of its spend into the next year is a timing change that matters to any finance officer tracking school capital against a fixed grant or borrowing envelope.
findings.figures: £600,000  2026/27 revised budget; £11,251 actual expenditure to date; £400,000 forecast outturn; (£200,000) forecast variance; £200,000 indicative 2027/28
